options.text: A replacement runtime that runs instead of JavaScript
A typed superset of JavaScript that compiles to plain JavaScript
A JavaScript library you import at runtime
A browser feature for validating data types

questions.explanation: TypeScript is a superset of JavaScript that adds a compile-time type layer and compiles down to ordinary JavaScript.

questions.prompt: What does it mean that TypeScript's types are "erased"?

options.text: They are checked again while the program runs
They are removed during compilation and have no runtime presence
They are stored in a separate file for the browser to read
They convert values to the declared type at runtime

questions.explanation: Type annotations exist only at compile time. The emitted JavaScript contains no types and performs no type checking of its own.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are jobs the TypeScript compiler (tsc) actually does? Select all that apply.

options.text: Type-checks your code and reports mismatches
Validates data types while the program runs
Changes the runtime behavior of correctly-typed code

questions.explanation: tsc type-checks and emits JavaScript. It does no runtime checking, and two programs differing only in annotations run identically.

questions.prompt: TypeScript decides type compatibility by an object's ______ rather than its declared name. (one word)
questions.explanation: TypeScript uses structural typing: any value with the required properties matches, regardless of what type it was declared as.

questions.prompt: What is the headline change in TypeScript 7.0?

options.text: A brand-new type system incompatible with 5.x
A native (Go) port of the compiler that is much faster, with the same language
Types are now checked at runtime
It removes support for JavaScript interop

questions.explanation: TypeScript 7.0 is a native port of the compiler written in Go — roughly ten times faster — while preserving the same language and type-checking rules.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.right: A compile-time note like ': string' that is erased
The compiler that type-checks and emits JavaScript

questions.explanation: Annotations are erased, tsc checks and emits, structural typing compares shapes, and TypeScript is a superset of JavaScript.
